_readme: Every hand-made asset the game knows how to use, other than card art.
Card art is deliberately NOT here: it binds by card id with no registration
step, and listing 296 filenames would be a second copy of data/cards to keep
in sync. Everything below is different — a fixed, small set the code refers
to by name, so naming it once and reading it from both the loader and the
verifier is what stops those two disagreeing.
A missing file is NOT an error. Every one of these degrades: icons fall back
to the procedural drawing the game has always used, boards fall back to the
flat clear colour, the logo falls back to the inline SVG. `npm run
verify:assets` reports coverage and only fails on a file that is present and
wrong — wrong size, wrong format, or one a browser cannot decode.
Sizes are exact and enforced. An icon that is 500x512 is a bug that shows up
as a hairline misalignment nobody can find later.
`minPx` is the one number that decides which artwork a player sees.
Every icon in this game exists twice: as one of these paintings, and as a
drawing on the 24-unit grid in `src/ui/art/uiIcons.ts` or
`src/ui/cardRenderer/icons.ts`. THE RULE IS: the painting is used at or
above `minPx`, and the drawing below it. One rule, one number per group,
read by the renderer, by the stylesheet and by `verify:art` alike.
The numbers are measured, not chosen. `npm run verify:art` renders each
group down a size ladder and the ladders are in
`scripts/screenshots/assets/audit/35-current-ladder.png` and `36-html-
ladder.png`: below `minPx` the strokes that identify a master have been
averaged away and every icon in the group is the same coloured smudge. A
card badge A/B at 7px (`31-badge-painted.png` against
`31-badge-procedural.png`) is the clearest case — the painted GALE loses
both outer swooshes and reads as a dark blob, while the drawn glyph reads
as wind.
The two sets are interchangeable at the same box, which is what makes one
number enough: every master here paints inside 84.4% of its frame, and the
drawn set is authored inside 83.3% of its 24-unit grid. Measured on all 40
files, not assumed.

assets.note: the HB monogram badge; every favicon and the .exe icon are downscales of this
the word HYPEBOUND, for the main menu

_minPx: The smallest box, in CSS pixels, at which a painting is still itself.
At or above it the painting is used; below it, the drawing.
Read off the size ladders, which are the measurement and not a taste:
`scripts/screenshots/assets/audit/36-html-ladder.png` renders all twelve
HTML icons at 12/15/18/24/32/48/72 and `35-current-ladder.png` does the
same for the eight Currents at 8 to 96. The size named is the first rung
at which the strokes that tell that icon apart from its neighbours are
still there.
currency 14 — a currency mark is a solid faceted gem, not linework, and
the whole job of a currency is to look precious. All four survive to 12
in the ladder; 14 is the size the game actually renders a wallet chip,
and the lobby at 17px is the proof (41-wallet.png).
ui 18 — the trophy, the bars, the packs and the flame all arrive by 18.
current 24 — cinder, pulse and tide read at 20; the group needs 24.
crest 28 — the size the starter picker already lists them at, where they
read as eleven distinct emblems.
confluence 28 — same artwork language as the crests, same number.
`minPxById` is for the outliers, because a group number is only as good
as its weakest member and rounding the whole group up to that member
would withdraw eleven perfectly legible paintings to protect three. Each
of these three is fine linework in a low-contrast tone:
mastery 32 — a thin grey laurel. On the lobby tile at 19px it is a smudge
and the drawn medal beats it outright; on the profile screen, which asks
for 40, the painting wins.
halo 32 — a hairline gold ellipse. Below 32 it is a dash.
prism 32 — a thin triangle with a fine rainbow. Below 32 it is a dash.

_note: One per faction, plus `default` for anything unfactioned and `boss` for
boss encounters. Chosen by the OPPONENT's faction, because the backdrop is
the place you have been dragged to, not the one you brought.
